title: Roxas Purple mangosteen (Roxas mangosteen): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Roxas Purple mangosteen: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Roxas Purple mangosteen is a mangosteen variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Roxas Purple is a registered mangosteen variety, also sold or known as Roxas mangosteen or NSIC Mt 02. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2006 as NSIC 2006 Mt 02. Marino Roxas bred it. Its record notes a yield of 850 fruits.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Roxas mangosteen or NSIC Mt 02, this is the same mangosteen. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [mangosteen variety finder](/crop-varieties), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).
Key facts about Roxas Purple mangosteen

blocks.caption: From the NSIC registry and its seller

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Roxas Purple was about 19 years old and about 7 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 850 fruits. It bears every year, with fruit in July August. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit mangosteen fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [thrips](/pests/thrips). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Roxas Purple weighs about 65.6 grams, and its shape is oblong. The flesh is snowy white and smooth. Its sweetness measured 21.4 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 27.2 percent of the fruit. The registry notes its fruiting season as July August, bearing annual.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Harvest:** Fruits July to August, annual bearer.
**Fruit:** About 66 g, purple rind, snowy white flesh, about 21.4 Brix.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: a Laguna farm mangosteen that bears yearly and is sweeter than UPLB Sweet (21.4 Brix). Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Roxas Purple mangosteen

Mangosteen is slow, often seven years or more to bear. Plant in deep, moist soil with some shade while young. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Roxas mangosteen the same as Roxas Purple?
items.a: Yes. Roxas mangosteen is another name for Roxas Purple, registered as NSIC 2006 Mt 02. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 850 fruits. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Roxas Purple?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
